- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤-0.4) or volatile, model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast for early periods.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day after sentiment drop.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period prices; cap forecast at 10–15% below true outcome’s final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
